issues.title: devblog automation: repair as a draft-generator (never auto-publish) -- post-league
issues.body:
Stacked for **after the Fri 2026-07-31 league launch**. Split out of the freeze-morning CI triage on 2026-07-29.

## Ruling that scopes this (Pip, 2026-07-29)

> "I dont want autogenerated devblog posts to be publiished, but the content is very usful for the publishing pipeline."

So this is NOT "make the workflow work again". The generator's *output* is wanted as raw material for human-authored posts; the *publishing* half must stay off permanently.

## What was done already (the holding fix)

`.github/workflows/dev-blog-automation.yml` is now **workflow_dispatch only** -- the `push: [main]` and `pull_request: [closed]` triggers were removed. That cleared a red that was firing on every single run of every branch and was drowning the "is CI green" signal on freeze day.

## Why the obvious two-line fix was refused

The visible failure is one missing dependency:

- `analyze-changes` installs `gitpython` (line 60).
- `create-dev-blog-entry` is a separate runner, sets up Python, then runs `import git` with no install step -> `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'git'`.

But that error is the only thing that has ever stopped this workflow from publishing:

1. `create-dev-blog-entry` ends in `git push` to `main`.
2. That push matches `sync-dev-blog.yml`'s `paths: dev-blog/entries/**` trigger.
3. `sync-dev-blog.yml` checks out `PipFoweraker/pdoom1-website` with `WEBSITE_SYNC_TOKEN` and pushes to its `main`.

Net: installing gitpython would have started auto-posting to the live public site on every merge.

## Second defect, never caught because the first one masks it

The entry body is built from triple-quoted strings indented inside a heredoc (roughly lines 218-274 pre-edit). Every emitted line carries 8 leading spaces, so the YAML frontmatter does not parse and the whole post renders as a single code block. The workflow has never produced an entry, so this has never been observed in the wild. The 50 files in `dev-blog/entries/` are human-authored (`git log -- dev-blog/` shows session captures and the music-session writeup, not automation output).

## Proposed shape

- [ ] Add the missing dependency install to `create-dev-blog-entry`.
- [ ] Fix the indent-mangled frontmatter/body generation; add a test or a golden-file check so a malformed entry cannot pass silently.
- [ ] **Remove the `git push` entirely.** Emit the generated material as a workflow artifact (or into a gitignored/scratch path), never a commit.
- [ ] Do NOT re-add the automatic `push`/`pull_request` triggers.
- [ ] Decide where the drafts land so they are genuinely usable as publishing-pipeline input rather than another thing to go stale.
- [ ] Replace `os.system('cd dev-blog && python generate_index.py')` with a checked subprocess call.

## Related

Rhymes with #1008 (release feed index is generated as an artifact and never committed back, so it is hand-maintained in practice). Both are "generated content that was meant to flow automatically, does not, and the gap got papered over by hand" -- worth a shared decision on which generated artifacts are allowed to auto-commit and which are draft-only.

issues.title: Release feed index is hand-maintained in practice: generated feed is uploaded as an artifact, never committed back
issues.body:
## Symptom

`public/releases/releases.json` (tracked) drifts from reality. Two instances found:

- v0.9.0 listed after the GitHub release was deleted (pruned by hand in #1006).
- v0.13.0 and v0.13.1 **missing** from the index despite both being tagged and released.

#1006 fixed the first instance by hand. This issue is the generator fix so it stops recurring.

## Root cause

`scripts/generate_release_metadata.py` rebuilds the ENTIRE index from git tags on every
run (`generate_releases_index`, line ~277) -- so CI already computes the correct index.
But `.github/workflows/enhanced-release.yml:213` only does `actions/upload-artifact` with
`path: public/releases/`. The correct feed is produced as a **build artifact and thrown
away**; nothing ever commits it back to the repo.

Net effect: the tracked index is hand-maintained, which is the documented rot anti-pattern
(cf. `docs/game-design/DQ_INDEX.md`, which is generated + gated by a `--check` pre-commit
hook -- that is the pattern to copy).

## Second defect: the detector is muted

`enhanced-release.yml:367-374` runs `verify_release_urls.py --sweep` with
`continue-on-error: true`. That is the same green-when-red mechanism PR #1007 just removed
from the simulation-tests job, one scope down at step level. The sweep also only runs
during a release workflow, so rot arising between releases is invisible until the next tag.

## Suggested fix (not prescriptive)

1. Commit the generated feed back on tag (or, cheaper and more in-house-style: add
   `generate_release_metadata.py --check` as a pre-commit + CI gate that fails when the
   tracked index differs from what the generator produces -- mirrors `sync_version.py --check`
   and `generate_dq_index.py --check`).
2. Make the `--sweep` step visible: either drop `continue-on-error` or surface its output
   the way #1007 surfaces sim-tier red. An old release 404ing should not block a NEW tag
   from shipping, so if it stays non-blocking it must at least be loudly reported.
3. Backfill v0.13.0/v0.13.1 into the index as part of the next version bump.

Found during the 2026-07-28 GitHub hygiene sweep; flagged (not silently regenerated) by the
#1006 lane.

issues.title: finance_engine desperation_payroll promises '-N doom now' but writes to the clobbered inert sink (silently never fires)
issues.body:
## Summary
Found during the ADR-0015 strip inventory (2026-07-27). The desperation_payroll financing offer (finance_engine.gd:254-264, accept_offer -> factory == 'desperation_payroll') calls state.add_resources({"doom": -suppress}) at line 258 and tells the player 'Pulled the desperation lever: -N doom now; a SECRET liability is planted' (line 264).

That doom write goes through the INERT sink: Resources.add() -> state.doom += value, which is clobbered every resolve by state.doom = doom_system.current_doom (turn_manager.gd:657). The promised immediate doom suppression never survives a resolve -- a live, player-reachable promise that silently does nothing.

## The fix pattern already exists
actions.gd:392-399 ('desperation_lever' quick action) is the already-fixed sibling: it routes the suppression through safety_absorption and deliberately omits any doom number from its message. finance_engine.gd is the stale duplicate that ADR-0015's original sweep missed (it only covered godot/data/).

## Scope
- Route the offer's suppression through the systemic channel (mirror actions.gd:392-399).
- Reword the offer message honestly.
- Before/after check: accepting the offer must produce a measurable doom-trajectory difference across a resolve, not just a transient print.

## Provenance
ADR-0015 inventory scout; recommended to ride the M half of the split strip errand (46 inert fields = S ticket; 20 live risk_events re-authors + this = M ticket). Related: ADR-0015, #613 prep docs, WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md section 5.

issues.title: feat(emit): calibration artifact — baseline p(Doom), sim 100%-topout date, ladder version (unblocks the website's doom clock + pdoom1-website#177)
issues.body:
**Artifact request from the pdoom1-website side.** Per cross-repo protocol v1 (Pip, 2026-07-26): the machine channel between repos is **artifacts, not prose**, and **pdoom1 owns game truth** while the website only *derives* presentation. The website needs a fact that no artifact currently carries, so this is an EMIT ask, not a request for numbers in a comment.

This is the last un-lodged blocker for the website's `/state-of-doom/` hero number and for pdoom1-website#177 (retiring three stubbed literals).

Searched pdoom1's open issues before filing (`calibration`, `baseline doom`, `emit artifact website`) — nothing covers this. Closest neighbours are #962 (frontier-labs list, a sibling not a duplicate) and #971/#986 (doom-stream balance work, which is the *input* to this calibration, not the emit).

---

## Why the website is asking rather than computing

Pip's ruling, captured in `pdoom1-website/docs/DOOM_CLOCK_AND_STATS_DESIGN.md`:

> **Direction of truth: the game leads.** The game's calibration is canonical; the website *derives and displays* it — it does not compute its own competing number.

So the website will not derive a p(Doom) figure of its own, ever. Today it ships literals instead, which is the thing being fixed:

`pdoom1-website/scripts/calculate-game-stats.py` writes into `public/data/version.json` → `game_stats`:

| field | current value | current provenance |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline_doom_percent` | `23` | literal in the script, comment says "Keep stubbed for now" |
| `strategic_possibilities` | `10000` | literal, comment says "Keep large number for now" |
| `frontier_labs_count` | `5` | counts a hardcoded list of lab names grepped out of `index.html`; `max(n, 5)` floor |

Those three are live on `https://pdoom1.com/data/version.json` right now. They are the website telling visitors a number the game did not produce. This repo's #962 (+ pdoom-data#37) already fixes the third. This issue asks for an artifact that fixes the first two and unlocks the hero clock.

## What is needed (three facts + provenance)

1. **Baseline p(Doom)** — the value a perfectly baseline run starts from / is tuned to.
2. **The 100%-topout date** — Pip's method, verbatim:
   > "Run a perfectly baseline simulation of p(Doom) and see when the engine naturally tops out at 100%. If it's past today's date, accept it and say 'this is super out of tune but we're going to update it every time we patch and we think it will hone in on a reasonable prediction reasonably quickly.'"
3. **The ladder/patch version the calibration corresponds to** — so the website can never show a number from one build next to a version stamp from another.

Plus enough provenance that the website can make the number *clickable into shown logic*. That is the whole design constraint of the page: "a number the reader can't interrogate is a number we don't ship." A bare float is not enough; the website has to be able to say how it was produced.

**"Foo" stays blank, deliberately.** Foo is the acknowledged fudge-factor between the pure baseline sim and lived game experience (it absorbs the rival, and the weirdness of the player being cast against actual people). Pip's call is that it is blank for now and the honest interim is to say so. So the artifact should carry the field as an explicit `null` with a note — **not** omit it, and **not** silently fold an unstated correction into the numbers. The website will render "no correction applied yet" rather than pretend the raw sim is a forecast. (Long-run replacement is an Institutional Brier Score; out of scope here.)

---

## The artifact

### Path (in-repo, source of truth)

```
godot/data/calibration.json
```

In `godot/data/` because that is where Epoch-versioned shaped data already lives, so the calibration diffs in the same PR as the balance change that moved it. Any stable path works — the website will read whatever is decided; what matters is that it is **fixed** and **committed**, not regenerated ad hoc.

### Publication (so a workflow can fetch it)

Attach the same file as a **release asset named exactly `calibration.json`** on every release, alongside the `releases.json` / `release_manifest.json` / `v0.13.1.json` assets already attached by `enhanced-release.yml`. That gives a permanent, unauthenticated, workflow-fetchable URL:

```
https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/releases/latest/download/calibration.json
```

GitHub redirects `releases/latest/download/<name>` to the newest release's asset of that name, so the website's fetch never needs a tag, never needs the API (no rate limit, no token), and **automatically stays coupled to the build players are actually running** — not to `main`. That coupling is the point: a calibration on `main` that has not shipped is not the number the player experienced.

`raw.githubusercontent.com/.../godot/data/calibration.json` is a fine secondary for anyone wanting the tip of `main`, but the release asset is the one the website will treat as canonical.

### Shape

Self-describing per this repo's own `docs/adr/0004-self-describing-data.md` — the file declares its schema so tooling dispatches on the declaration:

```json
{
  "schema_type": "game_calibration",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "generated_at": "2026-08-07T09:14:22Z",

  "version": {
    "game_version": "v0.14.0",
    "ladder_version": "L3",
    "commit": "409535dc0215d5e7bf4ff1b83025e8da98d7b4ef",
    "epoch": "2026-08"
  },

  "baseline": {
    "p_doom_start": 0.23,
    "p_doom_unit": "probability_0_to_1",
    "topout_date": "2031-04-18",
    "topout_turn": 174,
    "sim_start_date": "2026-08-07"
  },

  "foo": {
    "value": null,
    "status": "blank",
    "note": "Calibration fudge-factor between the pure baseline sim and lived game experience. Deliberately unset."
  },

  "provenance": {
    "method": "perfectly baseline simulation: no player actions beyond the forced minimum, default Balance values, no rival intervention",
    "seed": "baseline-2026-08",
    "runs": 1,
    "deterministic": true,
    "adr": "ADR-0006",
    "notes_url": "<link to wherever the method is written up in this repo; docs/balance/ looks like the natural home — this example URL is illustrative, not a claim the file exists>"
  },

  "game_stats": {
    "strategic_possibilities": 412,
    "strategic_possibilities_definition": "count of distinct player-selectable actions/upgrades reachable in a run",
    "frontier_labs_count": null,
    "frontier_labs_note": "delegated to #962 / pdoom-data#37; null until that lands"
  }
}
```

### Field notes (these are the bits that go wrong if left implicit)

- **`p_doom_unit` is not decoration.** `0.23` vs `23` is exactly the ambiguity that ships a 2300% doom figure to a visitor. Please emit the fraction and state the unit; the website does the formatting.
- **`topout_date` is a real-world calendar date**, not an in-sim turn count — that is what Pip's method produces and what a countdown can render. `topout_turn` + `sim_start_date` are included so the mapping is auditable and the website can show the working rather than assert the date.
- **Every numeric field must be nullable, and null must be emittable.** The website's rule is that a missing fact renders as a dash and never as a substituted literal — a default value ships precisely when the real lookup failed, which makes fallback literals the most dangerous kind. If a run does not top out at all, `topout_date: null` with a `provenance.note` is the correct output, and the page will honestly say so. Please do not emit a placeholder.
- **`strategic_possibilities` wants a definition string** because the website intends to link the number to the mechanic. `10000` is currently a shrug; `412, meaning <this>` is a fact a reader can check. Whatever the engine can actually count honestly is the right answer — a smaller true number beats a larger impressive one.
- **`runs: 1` is fine to start.** If a spread is cheap (p10/p50/p90 of topout across N baseline seeds) it is welcome as an optional `baseline.topout_date_spread`, but a single canonical deterministic run is what Pip's method describes and it is not worth blocking on.

### Versioning / cadence

- Regenerate on every release (Epoch minor bump and any patch that touches doom balance). The release asset carries the same version stamp as the build, so version skew is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.
- `schema_version` bumps only on a breaking shape change; the website will pin to `schema_version: 1` and fail loudly (dash + logged error) on an unrecognised value rather than guess.
- **Append-only history, strongly wanted, cheap:** the `/state-of-doom/` Tier-1 hero is a *rising series over time*, not a point. If each release also appends its `{version, generated_at, baseline}` record to a committed `godot/data/calibration_history.json` array, the website gets the series for free and it is authoritative. Without it the website can only accumulate the points it happens to observe from the release it fetched, which leaves holes for every release before adoption and any release it misses. One array append per Epoch.

---

## What the website does with it (so the shape can be sanity-checked against a real consumer)

1. A workflow fetches `releases/latest/download/calibration.json`.
2. `scripts/calculate-game-stats.py` stops writing literals: `baseline_doom_percent` and `strategic_possibilities` are read from the artifact, the hardcoded lab list is deleted (per #962), and every one of them becomes `null` → rendered as a dash on any fetch/parse failure.
3. `/state-of-doom/` Tier 1 renders the hero p(Doom) + the topout countdown, stamped with `version.game_version`, with the provenance block one click away.
4. `public/data/clocks.json` already reserves the slot — the `agi` clock carries `"calibration": {"provider": "game", "status": "pending"}` and renders "awaiting data" until this artifact exists. It will never render a guessed number.

## Related

- pdoom1-website#177 — de-stub `calculate-game-stats.py`; **blocked on this**.
- #962 + pdoom-data#37 — frontier-labs list; the sibling channel, deliberately not duplicated here.
- pdoom-data#38 — countdown-milestone dates; a different provider for a different tier.
- `pdoom1-website/docs/DOOM_CLOCK_AND_STATS_DESIGN.md` — the design capture this derives from, including the 2026-07-27 addendum ("dates are not hardcoded on the website").

No answer needed in prose. The artifact landing at a fetchable URL *is* the answer.

---
_Filed cross-repo by the pdoom1-website session under protocol v1 (Pip lifted the human-relay requirement for work items, 2026-07-26)._

issues.title: Bureaucratic tells: bodies telegraph doom via procedural anomaly (design, Wed W-block)
issues.body:
## Concept

From `SEED_GOVERNANCE_NAMES_YESAND.md` (2026-07-27 WS-3a Fable yes-and pass over the governance-body name pools): governance bodies should telegraph rising doom through PROCEDURAL ANOMALY, never printed numbers -- the honest replacement for the "-N doom" fiction strings the ADR-0015 data strip is deleting this week. Examples drafted:

- "The Sunday Group met on a Tuesday."
- "The Interim Interim Standards Board has requested a third interim."
- "The Panel moved to a larger room."
- "The Tribunal of Last Resort's waiting list has shortened."

This is one design motion with the ADR-0015 strip, not a separate feature: we remove fake numbers from event fiction, and tells are the true theatre derived from real sim state that replaces them (feed presents sim state; nothing reads back -- doctrine-clean per ADR-0015's single-authority rule).

## What needs design

A threshold -> anomaly mapping: which sim thresholds (doom bands, `global_alarm`/`global_panic` crossings, `political_pressure` sign flips, body `independence`/`teeth` values per `SEED_GOVERNANCE_BODIES_NAMES.md`'s tier structure) map to which procedural anomalies, and how tells are selected/rotated per body so the device doesn't repeat predictably.

## Slot

Wednesday agenda candidate (W-3b), per the yes-and doc's closing question: "Does the Wednesday workshop get 'bureaucratic tells' as a named agenda line (it wants 30 minutes)?"

Related: ADR-0015, ADR-0018, #984.

issues.title: ADR-0015 M-ticket: risk_events re-author + rebalance (20 live fields) + #967 finance fix + political_pressure dead-write
issues.body:
## Context

ADR-0015 (no printed doom deltas) shipped its engine layer, but the data migration is incomplete. The 2026-07-27 WS-3a scout audit (day-log: `docs/game-design/WS3A_DAYLOG_2026-07-27.md`; full inventory captured in the day's scratchpad `ADR0015_STRIP_INVENTORY.md`) found the literal-doom-field surface splits into two buckets with very different risk:

- **INERT (46 fields, S-sized):** `core_events.json` (40) + `2017.json` (4) + `crisis.json` (2). Path: `Resources.add()` -> `state.doom += value` -> **CLOBBERED every resolve** by `state.doom = doom_system.current_doom` (turn_manager.gd). Delete/re-author here is a pure no-op on balance. This bucket is BACKLOGGED per Pip 2026-07-27 1134 and is handled separately (S ticket, precedes the ADR-0016 pack schema).
- **LIVE (20 fields, this ticket, M-sized):** `risk_events.json` `pools.*.effects.doom` fields. Path: `turn_manager.gd` -> `doom_system.add_event_doom(amount, "risk_%s")` -- **NOT clobbered**, actively integrated every risk fire. These are the ticket this issue tracks.

## What this ticket covers

**Re-author the 20 live `risk_events.json` fields** -- this is a genuine balance change, not a mechanical strip:

- Each `pools.*.effects.doom` field needs a stream mapping (overhang / alarm / panic / political_pressure) with magnitude re-tuned to preserve the existing severity curve. Needs a playtest/calibration pass, not a same-day mechanical edit.
- All 20 also carry `"(+N doom)"` message strings that need rewording post-re-author (the printed-delta fiction ADR-0015 exists to remove).
- Line-numbered inventory of every field lives in the day's scout report (`ADR0015_STRIP_INVENTORY.md`, WS-3a session).

**Fold in the #967 fix.** `finance_engine.gd`'s `desperation_payroll` financing offer calls `state.add_resources({"doom": -suppress})` -- the same clobbered inert sink -- and prints "Pulled the desperation lever: -N doom now," a player-facing promise that silently never fires. The already-correct sibling is `actions.gd`'s `desperation_lever` quick action, which routes to `safety_absorption` and omits the doom number; `finance_engine.gd` is the stale duplicate ADR-0015 missed. Fix in the same PR as the re-author (same silent-promise class, same review).

**Fix the `political_pressure` double-dead write.** `actions.gd` (lobby_government action, current line ~618) writes `state.political_pressure += doom_reduction * Balance.num(...)` directly, but this write is clobbered every tick by `doom_system.gd`'s recompute (`state.political_pressure = _snap(state.global_alarm - state.global_panic)`, current line ~245) -- AND `political_pressure` is read by no gate or damper anywhere in the tree. It is doubly dead: the direct write never survives the tick, and even if it did, nothing consumes the value. Either wire a real consumer (a gate/damper reading `political_pressure`) or remove the dead direct-write and route lobbying's effect through the alarm/panic balance it's actually meant to shift.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

A17 / #971 (doom.streams.action_* pricing) is **explicitly NOT in this ticket** -- it already shipped in PR #974.

## Disposition

BACKLOGGED per Pip 2026-07-27 1134 (this is the M-ticket half of the R1 split ruling; the S ticket -- 46 inert fields + guard tests -- is separate and precedes the pack-schema work).

Related: ADR-0015, #967, #971.

issues.title: Half-day workshop: audit mechanics deep-dive (next epoch) -- something amazing under the smell
issues.body:
## Pip's ruling (2026-07-27 1811, verbatim intent)
'Make a firm plan to revisit audit mechanics next epoch. I will accept them for now but want a half-day workshop scheduled for it soon because it smells a little and I think there is something amazing and uplifting under it.'

## Context
The 4-way founder-hours ruling (2026-07-27, review-by 2026-08-31) shipped audits with unassigned researchers' optimistic self-reporting as the first distortion source (reported vs actual progress landed in the T1 substrate, PR #981). Accepted as first-pass; the smell = audits currently check only one lie from one source, and the mechanic's ceiling (Celine's-law channels, manager distortion, internal-board attestation chains, trust-as-resource) is clearly higher than its floor.

## The ask
Schedule a HALF-DAY workshop inside the v0.14 epoch (target window: week of 2026-08-10, before the 2026-08-31 formal review) on: what does auditing FEEL like as a player verb; the full distortion-source roster (self-reports, managers, boards, external attestations); audits x internal-board independence (the capture dial); whether trust becomes a first-class resource.

## Inputs to have ready
- Playtest observations of reported-vs-actual in the wild (Thursday 07-30 onward)
- The 2026-08-31 review question already on record: did optimistic self-reporting + audits earn its complexity?
- LADDER_0011 T4 atoms (manager shields, Celine's law) + governance-tier seed (internal board as audit destination)

Related: ADR-0011, #613, #980, PR #981.

issues.title: feat(engine): integrate frontier-labs dataset (pdoom-data#37); expose a list the website can pull to fix calculate-game-stats
issues.body:
## Ask (follow-on from pdoom-data#37)

Once pdoom-data ships its first-pass frontier-labs dataset (**PipFoweraker/pdoom-data#37** — foundation dates 2000→present), build the follow-on:

1. **Integrate** the frontier-labs list + foundation dates into the game engine (labs as timeline entities that come into existence on their founding dates).
2. **As soon as the MVP is enough for the website to consume it**, expose it so pdoom1-website can pull the list — so we can retire the hardcoded lab list in `calculate-game-stats.py` and drive `frontier_labs_count` (and future stats) from real data.

## Why

pdoom1-website currently hardcodes the frontier-labs list in `scripts/calculate-game-stats.py` to produce a stubbed count. Per the cross-repo protocol (game/data own truth; the website derives), that count should come from the canonical dataset. This also feeds the website's planned "state of doom" stats page.

## Sequencing (please don't block the website on full engine work)

`pdoom-data#37` → **engine integration** → **expose a consumable artifact**. The website does **not** need the full engine integration — it just needs a **stable, fetchable list** of `{id, name, founded, status}`. Please ship that consumable early (a served JSON, or simply point us at the pdoom-data serveable if that's cleaner) even if the richer engine timeline mechanics land later.

## Definition of done (for the website's needs)

- A documented, fetchable artifact of frontier labs + foundation dates.

issues.title: design(hiring): W3 -- revisit the candidate pool cap (MAX_CANDIDATES=6); stale once networking changes, and cap-hits are partly silent
issues.body:
Pip ruling (2026-07-26): the candidate pool cap needs revisiting in W3 if not before -- the cap may be stale as the way networking/sourcing works changes.

## Current state: MAX_CANDIDATES = 6, and it bites in several places

- `game_state.gd:104` -- `const MAX_CANDIDATES: int = 6`, hardcoded (NOT Balance-sourced, unlike most hiring tunables).
- `game_state.gd:597 add_candidate` -- **silently drops** the candidate when the pool is full. No log, no event.
- `hiring_pipeline.gd:186 _add_sourced_candidate` -- returns false at cap. The connections path emits a `connection_pool_full` event (hiring_pipeline.gd:719), but the ADVERTISE path just skips the `advertise_hit` event: **paid campaign candidates are silently discarded at cap**. This is the same failure mode that got the old free per-turn refill removed (see the NOTE at the top of turn_manager.gd) -- sourcing spend competing with a tiny fixed pool.
- `turn_manager.gd _restore_stranded_hires` (PR #960) -- a stranded hire returning to a FULL pool "takes another offer" (visible, but still a loss driven by the cap).
- `hiring_panel_controller.gd:120` -- UI header renders `CANDIDATE POOL (n/6)`.

## Questions for W3

- Is a fixed cap even the right shape once networking changes, or should pool size scale with something (reputation, org size, sourcing investment, an upgrade)?
- If a cap stays: what happens at cap must NEVER be silent -- displacement (worst candidate leaves), refusal-with-message, or a queue, but not a silent drop.
- First step regardless of the design ruling: move the constant to Balance (`hiring.pool_cap` or similar) so it is tunable data, not a const.

Related: #830 (hiring statefulness), #833 (people-and-money cohesion spine), #954 (full candidate cards -- a bigger pool changes that UI's scale assumptions).

issues.title: feat(ux): Surrender button on the in-game menu -- end run to leaderboard instead of abandoning
issues.body:
From Pip's 2026-07-26 playtest notes:

Add a quick SURRENDER button on the (in-game) menu:

- Lets a player END the run and go to the leaderboard with their score, instead of abandoning the session with nothing.
- Playtest-driven: people quitting mid-run currently just vanish; surrender converts an abandon into a leaderboard entry and a clean loop back to a new run.
- Rage-quit-friction principle applies: make ending gracefully EASIER than alt-F4.

Note: scene change must go through SceneTransition (repo MUST rule).

issues.title: design(narrative): mysterious-stranger messages delivered via an in-world basic PC (unlock/boot/password)
issues.body:
From Pip's 2026-07-26 playtest notes (design, downstream of the advisor-text lane):

Mysterious helpful stranger messages, delivered diegetically instead of appearing haphazardly:

- The game prompts "mysterious helpful stranger" text and needs a believable channel to get it to the player.
- Channel idea: the player unlocks (spends money on) a basic PC -- or starts with one -- and the stranger text renders ON that simulated PC screen.
- Optional juice: boot-up sequence and/or password mechanism on the PC, so acquiring the channel is itself a small beat.

Sequencing: build AFTER the advisor-text surface exists (advisor plumbing is the prerequisite delivery/text system). See the advisor-text issue.
